turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: In terms of cognitive processing, research suggests that our brains treat spoken and unspoken words similarly. The McGurk effect, for example, shows that when we see a speaker's lips say one word but hear another, our brains combine the two to create a third, intermediate sound. So, in a way, yes, inaudible words are processed similarly to visual words, even if they aren't consciously perceived.
